text: Northbridge Retail now has real Azure and AWS infrastructure under Terraform. This chapter is about running that safely as a whole platform team, starting with how to manage dev, staging, and production without three copies of the same configuration.

A workspace lets the same .tf files run against multiple, completely separate state files, switched with a command. Every configuration starts in a default workspace, and you can create more — each one gets its own isolated state.

The terraform.workspace expression lets one set of files behave differently per workspace. This resource group name includes the current workspace, so dev and staging get different real Azure resource names from the exact same file.

Workspaces share the same files, defaults, and provider config across every environment, which means one typo in a workspace select command can point an apply meant for staging straight at production. Northbridge's team chose directory-per-environment instead — separate folders, each with its own backend and tfvars, calling the same shared modules. Workspaces still earn their place for short-lived, low-risk scenarios like a feature-branch preview.
With environments sorted out, next up is Lesson 30: running Terraform from a CI/CD pipeline instead of someone's laptop.
